title: Airline On-Time Record for My Flights
dataSources: ADS-B aircraft snapshots (`adsb:aircraft`), personal flight logbook (`flight:log`), commute trips (`commute:trip`), transit arrivals (`transit:arrival`), geofence events (`geofence:event`), travel documents (`travel:document`), fare quotes (`airprice:quote`).
app: Home ADS-B receiver (dump1090 / readsb / tar1090 JSON feed), personal flight logbook exports, commute/transit APIs, and phone geofence webhooks via Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=flight:log
| eval delay_min=round((actual_dep_epoch-sched_dep_epoch)/60,0)
| stats avg(delay_min) as avg_delay, sum(eval(if(delay_min>15,1,0))) as late, count as flights by airline
| eval on_time_pct=round(100*(flights-late)/flights,1)
| sort on_time_pct
description: Calculates the on-time percentage of the airlines you actually fly, not the industry averages that never match your luck.
value: Your personal on-time record beats any published statistic when choosing who to book next, especially for tight connections.
implementation: Record scheduled versus actual departure per flight; schedule monthly and rank the airlines you use by on-time rate.
visualization: Bar chart of on-time percentage by airline with average delay.
grandmaExplanation: It works out how often the airlines you use actually leave on time, based on your own flights rather than general figures.
